name: Zibeon
overview: Zibeon is a male figure identified as a Hivite in the Scriptures. He is notably recognized as the grandfather of Oholibamah, who became one of Esau's wives, situating him within the genealogical context of the early biblical narrative. Beyond these details, Scripture provides limited additional information about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Zibeon is a proper name meaning "hyena." This name is not indicated as being given by God, but it is recorded in Genesis 36:2, reflecting a distinctive personal designation within the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Zibeon is recorded as the grandfather of Judith, an inferred relationship based on genealogical data in Genesis 36:2. Scripture does not provide further details about his family connections beyond those related to his granddaughter Oholibamah and Judith.
scriptureSignificance: Zibeon's significance in the biblical narrative primarily arises from his role as an ancestor connected to Esau through his granddaughter Oholibamah, linking him to the lineage of Edomite descendants. This connection situates him within the broader framework of Israel's neighboring peoples and their genealogies, contributing to the historical and relational context of the patriarchal accounts.
